title: Limits and affine sections of surjective quasi-coherent towers
statement: Use algebraic spaces over a scheme $S$ and their small etale sites and structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Module sheaves and quasi-coherence are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Write $D(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for its full subcategory of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. Let $(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge1}$ be an inverse sequence of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-modules with surjective transition morphisms, on an algebraic space $Z$ over $S$. Let $\mathcal M=\varprojlim_n\mathcal M_n$ be the sectionwise inverse limit [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. For the right derived inverse limit of this strict tower, the canonical map $\mathcal M[0]\to R\varprojlim_n\mathcal M_n[0]$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-weil-derived-limit]; the inverse limit need not be quasi-coherent. For every affine scheme $U$ etale over $Z$, the maps $\mathcal M_{n+1}(U)\to\mathcal M_n(U)$ are surjective, $H^p(U_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal M_n|_U)=0$ and $H^p(U_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal M|_U)=0$ for $p>0$. Here $H^p$ denotes the right derived functors of sections on the indicated slice etale site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 0D3E (lemma-Rlim-quasi-coherent), (2), (3), and its proof for affine etale objects (surjectivity on sections and affine acyclicity).

proof.text: Take $\mathcal B$ to be the affine schemes etale over $Z$. Every scheme object $V\to Z$ has an affine open covering, whose members are still etale over $Z$, so this collection covers every object, with no quasi-compactness assumption on $Z$. On localization at $U\to Z$ the ringed etale site and structure sheaf are those of $U$: an object is a scheme over $U$ with its given composite to $Z$, and the coverings and ring sections agree. Restrict the local free presentations defining quasi-coherence to this localized site. Thus every $\mathcal M_n|_U$ is quasi-coherent. Restriction on module sheaves is exact, so the transition maps remain epimorphisms on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$.

source.place: Tag 0D3E, proof, choice of the collection of affine etale objects.

proof.text: All these sites have small skeletons in the fixed coefficient universe. Their module categories are Grothendieck abelian and hence have enough injectives. Apply the ringed-site module/abelian evaluation comparison, and the comparison with evaluation at the final object of a slice. Consequently the module cohomology over $U$ in the item agrees with the abelian cohomology of the underlying sheaf on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. These comparisons apply to arbitrary structure-ring sheaves, not merely constant coefficient rings.

source.place: Tags 03FD (module/abelian cohomology) and 03F3 (cohomology of a localization).

proof.text: For any quasi-coherent $E$ on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, the Zariski/etale quasi-coherent equivalence writes $E\simeq F_{\mathrm{et}}$ for a quasi-coherent Zariski module $F$, preserving its sections on opens. The natural cohomology comparison identifies $H^p(U_{\mathrm{et}},E)$ with $H^p(U,F)$. Since $U$ is affine, affine vanishing gives zero for $p>0$. Apply this first to each $E=\mathcal M_n|_U$; it will also apply to the transition kernels in the next step.

source.place: Tag 0D3E, proof, first vanishing assertion; spaces-cohomology.tex Section higher-direct-image; descent.tex Tag 03DW; coherent.tex Tag 01XB.

proof.text: Fix $n$ and affine etale $U\to Z$. Set $E=\mathcal M_{n+1}|_U$, $G=\mathcal M_n|_U$ and $K=\ker(E\to G)$. The scheme-etale kernel lemma makes $K$ quasi-coherent. The restricted transition is epic by step 1, so $0\to K\to E\to G\to0$ is short exact in module sheaves. Its derived-section exact sequence contains $E(U)\to G(U)\to H^1(U,K)$. The last term vanishes by step 3, proving $\mathcal M_{n+1}(U)\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal M_n(U)$. No assumption of surjectivity on all sections was substituted for the assumed surjectivity of the transition morphism.

source.place: Tag 0D3E, proof, assertion of surjectivity of affine sections; descent.tex Tag 06VE and sites-cohomology.tex long exact cohomology sequence.

proof.text: Fix $U\in\mathcal B$ and write $A_n=\mathcal M_n(U)$ with transitions $f_n:A_{n+1}\to A_n$, surjective by step 4. By the cited Roos computation, $R^1\varprojlim_nA_n\cong\operatorname{coker}(1-s)$, where $(1-s)(x_n)_n=(x_n-f_n(x_{n+1}))_n$ on $\prod_nA_n$. We show $1-s$ is surjective. Given $(y_n)_n\in\prod_nA_n$, put $x_1=0$ and, once $x_n$ is chosen, choose $x_{n+1}\in A_{n+1}$ with $f_n(x_{n+1})=x_n-y_n$, possible since $f_n$ is surjective. Then $x_n-f_n(x_{n+1})=y_n$ for every $n$, so $(1-s)(x_n)_n=(y_n)_n$. Hence $R^1\varprojlim_n\mathcal M_n(U)=0$. This uses no finiteness of the section groups.

source.place: Tag 07KW (lemma-compute-Rlim), proof of clause (3) specialized to surjective transition maps; Roos computation of R^1 lim as coker(1-s).

proof.text: Apply the covering-collection criterion to $(Z_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_Z)$ and $\mathcal B$. Its covering hypothesis is step 1, its positive-degree stage acyclicity is step 3, and its vanishing $R^1\lim$ hypothesis is step 5. Its ordinary limit is exactly $\mathcal M$, since module-sheaf limits are sectionwise. It gives the asserted natural isomorphism $\mathcal M[0]\to R\varprojlim_n\mathcal M_n[0]$ and $H^p(U_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal M|_U)=0$ for every affine etale $U$ and $p>0$. Together with steps 3 and 4 these are all positive assertions of the item; none asserts that this limit is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Tag 0D3E, final sentence of proof, applying sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0BKY.

proof.text: For the warning, take $Z=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]$ over a field $k$, and let $\mathcal M_n=(\widetilde{k[t]/(t^n)})_{\mathrm{et}}$. The tilde section formula gives global sections $k[t]/(t^n)$ and zero sections on $D(t)$; the etale equivalence preserves these open sections. The quotient transitions are epimorphisms: tilde preserves cokernels by its adjunction, and passage to the etale site is exact. Thus $\mathcal M(Z)=\lim_n k[t]/(t^n)$ is the module of formal coefficient sequences $k[[t]]$, whereas $\mathcal M(D(t))=0$. If $\mathcal M$ were quasi-coherent, its Zariski restriction would be quasi-coherent and affine section base change would give $\mathcal M(D(t))=k[[t]][1/t]$. The latter is nonzero: no power of $t$ kills the series $1$. This contradiction proves the warning without any claim of quasi-coherence for infinite products.
